title: Slow English Podcast #123: Antigua and Barbuda

sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emily, I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Antigua and Barbuda.
It is a small island country in the Caribbean Sea.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Antigua and Barbuda is in the Caribbean.
It is east of Puerto Rico and north of Guadalupe.
It is made of two main islands, Antigua and Barbuda.
There are also some small islands.
The capital city is St. John's.
It is on the island of Antigua.
St. John's has colorful buildings, markets,
Barbuda is smaller and has few people,
but many birds and beautiful beaches.
About 100,000 people live in Antigua and Barbuda.
The country is peaceful and friendly.
Many people speak Caribbean English with a local accent.
It is easy to understand and full of warm expressions.
The weather is warm and sunny all year.
It is usually around 25 to 30 degrees Celsius.
The dry season from December to April.
The rainy season from May to November.
There can be hurricanes between August and October.
The country has white sand beaches,
one for every day of the year.
You can see frigate birds with red chests,
goats, donkeys and chickens on farms.
The Codderington Lagoon is a special bird sanctuary.
The food is fresh tropical and flavorful.
People eat fish, lobster and conch,
fruits like mangoes, pineapples and bananas,
People drink water and fresh juice,
sorrel, a red drink made from flowers,
Adults may drink rum punch or local beer.
Cold drinks are popular because of the warm weather.
People enjoy talking with friends and neighbors,
People are friendly and say hello with a smile.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Emancipation Day and other national events.
Some fun facts about Antigua and Barbuda.
The frigate bird is the national bird.
The islands were once a British colony.
Antigua and Barbuda is famous for cricket.
Now you know many things about Antigua and Barbuda.
what people eat and how they live.
